premise: The user supplies a short account combining an observed event with their opinion of it.
mechanism: Separate the observation from the judgment, then help rewrite the account without losing either.

premise: The user supplies a short fictional passage and wants an open-ended discussion question.
mechanism: Create a question anchored in the passage, then revise it to allow more than one defensible response.

premise: The user supplies a short description of a craft but omits how two pieces are joined.
mechanism: Identify the gap, offer clearly labelled possibilities, then adapt once the user specifies the join.

premise: The user supplies two versions of a fictional paragraph and asks what changed in tone.
mechanism: Compare concrete wording in both versions, then discuss whether the plot facts also changed.

premise: The user supplies a short memoir excerpt where the narrator is unsure who first suggested an idea.
mechanism: Preserve the uncertainty in a summary, then discuss how a definitive rewrite would alter the meaning.

premise: The user wants a relaxed craft afternoon with a friend who enjoys making different things.
mechanism: Build a flexible shared setup, then accommodate the friend's stated preference for independent projects.

premise: The user wants to make family story time more participatory without requiring anyone to perform.
mechanism: Suggest optional prompts and a listening role, then adapt to the ages and preferences the user provides.

premise: The user wants to sort a crowded wardrobe in manageable stages.
mechanism: Agree on a category-based sequence, then revise it to avoid making a large pile on the floor.

premise: Two friends want to read the same short story and discuss it casually.
mechanism: Plan a flexible discussion around a few questions, then accommodate different reading speeds.

premise: The user wants to draw with a beginner friend without turning the session into a lesson.
mechanism: Suggest a shared subject and optional observations, then adjust to the friend's preferred materials.

premise: The user wants to rearrange a small room to create a reading area.
mechanism: Ask about movable furniture and light, then propose a layout respecting an item that must stay put.

premise: The user and a friend want to exchange basic craft skills in one informal session.
mechanism: Divide time between demonstrations and practice, then adjust when one person prefers to watch first.

premise: The user wants a screen-free visit with relatives who have varied interests.
mechanism: Develop a few optional activities, then adjust around a relative who prefers conversation to games.

premise: The user wants to photograph everyday objects at home as a small creative project.
mechanism: Choose a theme and a loose sequence, then retain the user's preference for natural-looking arrangements.

premise: The user wants to make a small personal zine from drawings and brief notes.
mechanism: Plan page roles and assembly, then adapt when the user wants the drawings to dominate.
